original_question: Determine the exact enumeration and asymptotic growth of permutations that avoid the classical pattern 1324. In particular, determine the Stanley-Wilf limit for 1324-avoiding permutations and, if possible, an exact formula or asymptotic description for the number of 1324-avoiders of length n.
target_in_paper: Section 3, "Enumeration and asymptotics of avoiders: The case of 1324," specifically the survey’s central unresolved problem of determining the exact enumeration and asymptotic growth of the classical pattern-avoidance class Av(1324), including the value of its Stanley-Wilf limit. The abstract and introduction also single this out as the first major topic of the paper. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.7320))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s main unresolved problem in its 1324 section: counting 1324-avoiding permutations, understanding their asymptotic growth, and isolating the Stanley-Wilf limit as the key exponential growth constant. It also stays within the intended scope of the paper—classical single-pattern avoidance for 1324, rather than a broader family of patterns. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.7320))
missing_details: The ambient objects should be specified explicitly: permutations in S_n avoiding the classical pattern 1324, not vincular, bivincular, or mesh avoidance. Section 3 says that, unless otherwise noted, the remainder of the paper is about classical patterns. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))

The counting function should be named explicitly, e.g. Av_n(1324)={π∈S_n: π avoids 1324} and s_n(1324)=|Av_n(1324)|. The draft currently refers informally to “the number of 1324-avoiders of length n” without fixing notation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))

The Stanley-Wilf limit should be written precisely as L(1324)=lim_{n→∞} s_n(1324)^{1/n}. The paper notes that existence of this limit is already known in general for classical patterns, so the unresolved issue is its value for 1324, not its existence. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))

To be paper-faithful, the problem should mention that 1324 represents the only Wilf class of classical patterns of length 4 for which neither exact enumeration nor asymptotics are known. That context explains why this problem is singled out. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))

The phrase "if possible" is too vague. A sharper hierarchy is: determine s_n(1324) exactly; failing that, determine an exact asymptotic formula; at minimum, determine the exponential growth constant L(1324). This matches the paper’s framing of the unresolved issues. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))

The draft should not be narrowed to the auxiliary inversion-count conjecture discussed via [23]; in this survey that conjecture is presented only as a possible route to an upper bound on the Stanley-Wilf limit, not as the primary open problem being highlighted. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
refined_question: For each n≥1, let Av_n(1324)={π∈S_n: π avoids the classical pattern 1324} and let s_n(1324)=|Av_n(1324)|. Determine s_n(1324) exactly; failing that, determine an exact asymptotic formula for s_n(1324) as n→∞. In particular, determine the value of the Stanley-Wilf limit L(1324)=lim_{n→∞} s_n(1324)^{1/n}, i.e. the exponential growth rate of the unique unresolved Wilf class of classical permutation patterns of length 4 represented by 1324. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1210.7320))
justification: The draft is aiming at the survey’s first featured open problem. The abstract says the paper first surveys “the enumeration and asymptotics of the pattern 1324,” and the introduction announces Section 3 as treating 1324 because it is the shortest classical pattern whose avoidance is still unknown asymptotically. Section 3 then states that 1324 is the only Wilf class of patterns of length 4 for which neither exact enumeration nor asymptotics have been determined, and discusses the Stanley-Wilf limit, bounds, and conjectural evidence. That makes the right refined question the direct one about the exact sequence s_n(1324) and its asymptotics, rather than the narrower inversion-count conjecture from the cited paper [23]. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.7320))
